A Vue child component has an 'items' prop for a todo list. A button handler currently does `props.items.push(newItem)` to add an item. What should this do instead so the parent's data stays in sync?

trialRecords.output:
The child must not mutate the prop. Vue only warns about it at runtime, but the real problem is architectural: the child doesn't own that array, the parent does, and an in-place `push` is invisible to anyone reading the parent. Replace the mutation with an emit and let the parent apply the change.

**1. Declare the emit (type-only form, matching the rest of the `<script setup>`):**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { TodoItem } from '@/types'

const props = defineProps<{
  items: TodoItem[]
}>()

const emit = defineEmits<{
  'add-item': [item: TodoItem]
}>()

function handleAdd(): void {
  emit('add-item', { id: crypto.randomUUID(), text: 'New todo', done: false })
}
</script>
```

Use `defineEmits<{ 'add-item': [item: TodoItem] }>()` (the tuple form) rather than the old `(e: 'add-item', item: TodoItem) => void` call-signature form — that is the current type-only style and it gives you a typed payload the parent can be checked against.

**2. The parent owns the state and handles the event:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import TodoList from './TodoList.vue'
import type { TodoItem } from '@/types'

const items = ref<TodoItem[]>([])

function addItem(item: TodoItem): void {
  items.value.push(item) // parent mutates its own ref — this is fine
}
</script>

<template>
  <TodoList :items="items" @add-item="addItem" />
</template>
```

**If it's a two-way binding, use `v-model` instead of a bespoke event.** If the parent wrote `<TodoList v-model:items="items" />`, the child declares a `modelValue`-style prop plus a matching `update:` emit and emits rather than pushes:

```ts
const props = defineProps<{ items: TodoItem[] }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{ 'update:items': [items: TodoItem[]] }>()

function addItem(item: TodoItem): void {
  emit('update:items', [...props.items, item])
}
```

Note the spread: emit a *new array* rather than `props.items.concat()` mutated in place, so the parent sees a genuinely new value and any `watch`/`computed` on it re-evaluates cleanly.

**If several unrelated components need to add to this list**, the array shouldn't live in a single parent at all — move it into a Pinia store and have the child call a `store.addItem(item)` action. The child then mutates nothing and imports no prop; the store owns the array and is the single source of truth. A component that both displays the list and adds to it, with other screens also touching the list, is the signal to promote it to a store.

Two things to watch when you make the change:

- Don't reach into the prop and call `push` even "temporarily" to see it work — it will appear to work in dev and then warn or desync once the parent re-renders from its own path.
- If `items` is destructured somewhere in the child (`const { items } = props`), on Vue below 3.5 that destructure breaks reactivity entirely, so the emitted-only approach plus reading `props.items` directly avoids that trap too.

After the change, run `npx vue-tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint .` — a leftover `props.items.push` will usually also trip an `eslint-plugin-vue` mutation-related rule, which is a useful confirmation the fix is complete.

// after
